meta.plant_name: Roswell Information Park Data Center power station

Status Detail.value: ALQ42026: "Kameir said the company plans to start building 700 megawatts of natural-gas power to be ready for commercial data center operations in the fourth quarter of 2028. He said the company has an offer on a 736-megawatt gas plant, "but the equipment hasn't been secured." Gas will come from the San Juan Basin and elsewhere." From Yahoo!. Check whether capacity changes/increases.
Status Detail.note:
This is the text already in the box, left unchanged so that the link can be added.

Source:

- Open the Albuquerque Journal story at https://www.abqjournal.com/business/data-center-developers-are-eyeing-new-mexico-will-they-be-welcomed/3147510, published October 25, 2026. Go to the section on the Roswell information park. It quotes the developer's interim chief executive, Chris Kameir: 'the company has an offer on a 736-megawatt gas plant, but the equipment hasn't been secured.'
- The 736 MW offer is for a plant, not a change of the plan. The plan stated is still 700 MW, so the capacity stays 700 MW.
- The story is behind a paywall, and the address loads with the words 736 and Roswell Information Park.

Backup Power.note:
Backup power:

- The Albuquerque Journal story at https://www.abqjournal.com/business/data-center-developers-are-eyeing-new-mexico-will-they-be-welcomed/3147510 says the developer will 'start building 700 megawatts of natural-gas power' for data center operations, and discusses state microgrid rules, meaning power 'not hooked into regional grids'.
- That makes the gas plant the main power supply, not an emergency backup. No permit or other document gives an engine list.
- This is implied by the article and not stated in one sentence, so the confidence is medium.

units.notes: I found no permit, county record or news story that names the turbine type, the maker or the number of engines. The only source is the October 2026 news story. The project is moving, so Latest Activity is left alone.

Latitude.note: The only place named is the city of Roswell. I moved the point from downtown, where GEM's point sits in the middle of the main street, to open desert ground about 1 km north-east of the city center. The imagery date is unknown.

Longitude.note: See the Latitude note. The point is an approximate placeholder in open ground near Roswell.

Location accuracy.note: No source gives a parcel or an address. The city of Roswell agenda at https://www.roswell-nm.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_02032026-2981 and the news story at https://www.abqjournal.com/business/data-center-developers-are-eyeing-new-mexico-will-they-be-welcomed/3147510 name only the city.

qa.question: Should capacity stay 700 MW given the 736 MW plant offer?
qa.finding: The story at https://www.abqjournal.com/business/data-center-developers-are-eyeing-new-mexico-will-they-be-welcomed/3147510 says the company will build 700 megawatts and has an offer on a 736-megawatt gas plant.
qa.recommendation: Keep 700 MW. Change it only if a permit or a signed purchase names a different electrical size.
qa.note: One tracker lists 200 MW for this campus, but I did not use it because it gives no document. The city agenda at https://www.roswell-nm.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_02032026-2981 names the campus but gives no megawatts. The agenda is a scanned PDF that the verifier could not read, so I did not cite it.

qa.question: Does any document state the turbine technology for the Roswell plant?
qa.finding: I searched the October 2026 news story, the city of Roswell agendas and a web search for the developer. None names a turbine or engine type.
qa.recommendation: Leave Turbine/Engine Technology as unknown and check again when an air permit application appears.
qa.note: No air permit for this plant was found in the state record harvest.
